stem.en: The Gurjara-Pratihāras, the Pālas and the Rāṣhṭrakūṭas fought for control of Kannauj. What did their systems of administration have in common?

text.en: Each abolished its provinces during the fighting and ruled its villages from the capital.
Each copied the Chola system of drawing names from a pot.
Each gave all its power to the village assemblies and had no king.
All three mixed monarchy with decentralised units, and in all three the village was the smallest, largely self-reliant unit.

explanation.en: The administrative systems of all three kingdoms followed the same pattern: a mix of monarchy and decentralised units of provinces, districts and villages. In all cases the village remained the smallest administrative unit and was largely self-reliant in infrastructure, social welfare and education.

hints.en: Who won Kannauj does not matter for this question.
Look for what was true of the village in all three.
